name: Amber Fort (Amer Fort)
description: Magnificent 16th-century hilltop fort combining Hindu and Mughal architecture. UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of Hill Forts of Rajasthan.

name: Hawa Mahal
description: Iconic 'Palace of Winds' built in 1799 with 953 small windows. Five-storey pink sandstone facade is the most photographed landmark in Jaipur.

name: City Palace, Jaipur
description: Sprawling palace complex blending Rajasthani and Mughal architecture. Houses a museum with royal artifacts, textiles, and weapons.

name: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
description: UNESCO World Heritage astronomical observation site built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in 1734. Contains the world's largest stone sundial.

name: Nahargarh Fort
description: 18th-century fort overlooking Jaipur city. Offers panoramic views and houses the Madhavendra Bhawan palace with unique interconnected suites.

name: Jaigarh Fort
description: Massive 18th-century fort known for housing the world's largest cannon on wheels, Jaivana. Connected to Amber Fort by underground passage.

name: Albert Hall Museum
description: The oldest museum in Rajasthan, built in Indo-Saracenic style. Houses an extensive collection of paintings, sculptures, and decorative arts.

name: Jal Mahal
description: 18th-century 'Water Palace' situated in the middle of Man Sagar Lake. Stunning example of Rajput architecture, viewable only from shore.

name: City Palace, Udaipur
description: Largest palace complex in Rajasthan, built over 400 years by successive rulers. Overlooks Lake Pichola with stunning architecture.

name: Lake Pichola
description: Artificial lake created in 1362, surrounded by palaces and hills. Boat rides offer views of Jag Mandir and Lake Palace.

name: Jagdish Temple
description: Grand Indo-Aryan temple built in 1651, dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Features intricate carvings and a large brass image of Garuda.

name: Saheliyon-ki-Bari
description: 18th-century ornamental garden with fountains, marble pavilions, and lotus pools. Built for royal ladies-in-waiting.

name: Fateh Sagar Lake
description: Scenic artificial lake surrounded by hills. Popular for boating and houses Nehru Garden on an island.

name: Mehrangarh Fort
description: One of India's largest and most imposing forts, perched 400 feet above Jodhpur. Houses an excellent museum with royal palanquins and armour.

name: Jaswant Thada
description: White marble cenotaph built in 1899, known as the 'Taj Mahal of Marwar'. Features intricate carvings and overlooks Mehrangarh Fort.

name: Umaid Bhawan Palace
description: One of the world's largest private residences, built between 1929-1943. Part is a luxury hotel, part museum, part royal residence.

name: Clock Tower & Sardar Market
description: Iconic clock tower at the heart of Jodhpur's old city. Surrounded by vibrant Sardar Market selling spices, textiles, and handicrafts.

name: Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Quila)
description: UNESCO World Heritage 'Golden Fort' built in 1156. One of the few living forts in the world with shops, hotels, and homes inside.

name: Sam Sand Dunes
description: Vast expanse of golden sand dunes 42km from Jaisalmer. Famous for camel safaris, desert camping, and stunning sunsets.

name: Patwon Ki Haveli
description: Cluster of five ornate havelis built between 1805-1862 by a wealthy Jain merchant. Features the finest stone carving in Jaisalmer.

name: Kuldhara Abandoned Village
description: Mysterious abandoned village from the 13th century. Over 80 families left overnight, leaving the village eerily intact.

name: Pushkar Lake
description: Sacred lake surrounded by 52 bathing ghats and over 400 temples. One of the holiest pilgrimage sites in Hinduism.

name: Brahma Temple, Pushkar
description: One of very few temples in the world dedicated to Lord Brahma. The 14th-century temple is one of Pushkar's most significant landmarks.

name: Ajmer Sharif Dargah
description: Sufi shrine of Moinuddin Chishti, one of India's most important Muslim pilgrimage sites. Attracts millions of visitors annually.

name: Ana Sagar Lake
description: Artificial lake created in 1135 AD by Anaji Chauhan. Scenic promenade with marble pavilions built by Emperor Shah Jahan.

name: Chittorgarh Fort
description: India's largest fort by area (700 acres), UNESCO World Heritage Site. Legendary symbol of Rajput valor with palaces, temples, and towers.

name: Dilwara Jain Temples
description: 11th-15th century marble Jain temples renowned for incredibly detailed and intricate marble carvings, considered among the finest in India.

name: Nakki Lake
description: Scenic lake at Mount Abu surrounded by hills and rocks. Popular for boating and sunset views at Toad Rock viewpoint.

name: Guru Shikhar
description: Highest point in Rajasthan at 1,722 metres (5,650 ft). Part of the Aravalli Range with panoramic views and a temple at the summit.

name: Junagarh Fort
description: 16th-century fort unique for being built on flat ground (not a hilltop). Houses palaces, temples, and a museum with rich collections.

name: Karni Mata Temple (Rat Temple)
description: Famous temple housing thousands of sacred rats (kabbas). Located in Deshnoke, 30km from Bikaner. Unique religious experience.

name: Ranthambore National Park
description: One of India's best tiger reserves. Famous for diurnal tiger sightings amid ancient ruins. Home to diverse wildlife and the historic Ranthambore Fort.

name: Ranthambore Fort
description: 10th-century fort within Ranthambore National Park. UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of Hill Forts of Rajasthan.

name: Kumbhalgarh Fort
description: 15th-century Mewar fort with the second-longest wall in the world (36 km). UNESCO World Heritage Site with panoramic Aravalli views.

name: Ranakpur Jain Temple
description: 15th-century Jain temple with 1,444 intricately carved marble pillars, no two alike. One of the five major Jain pilgrimage sites.

name: Taragarh Fort, Bundi
description: 14th-century hillside fort known for its massive ramparts and large reservoir. Features Bhim Burj, a famous large cannon.

name: Bundi Palace (Garh Palace)
description: Grand Rajput palace complex famous for its stunning Bundi-school miniature paintings on palace walls. Often called a 'mini-Jaipur'.

name: Keoladeo National Park (Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary)
description: UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the world's premier birding areas. Home to over 350 species of birds, especially winter migrants.

name: Sariska Tiger Reserve
description: Tiger reserve in the Aravalli hills, closest to Delhi. Home to reintroduced Bengal tigers, leopards, and diverse birdlife.

name: Mandawa Havelis
description: Open-air art gallery of painted havelis in the Shekhawati region. 18th-19th century merchant mansions with elaborate frescoes.

name: Osian Temples
description: Cluster of 8th-11th century Hindu and Jain temples in the Thar Desert. Known as the 'Khajuraho of Rajasthan' for their sculptural beauty.

name: Desert National Park
description: One of the largest national parks in India, showcasing Thar Desert ecosystem. Home to the endangered Great Indian Bustard.

name: Shrinathji Temple
description: 17th-century Vaishnavite temple housing the sacred idol of Lord Krishna (Shrinathji). One of India's most visited temples.

name: Haldighati
description: Historic mountain pass where the famous Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between Maharana Pratap and Mughal forces. Features a museum and Chetak memorial.

name: Sambhar Salt Lake
description: India's largest inland salt lake, a Ramsar wetland site. Important habitat for flamingos and migratory birds. Salt production since the 6th century.
